context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It guarantees strict regional data residency and compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US)
- Licensed Clinicians
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (GCP regions: `europe-west3`, `us-central1`)
- National E-Prescription Networks (EU) & US Pharmacy Systems
- WebRTC SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit) Media Relay
- Break-Glass Identity Provider (IdP)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform: HTTPS / WebRTC (TLS 1.3, adaptive below 300 kbit/s)
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (EU) -> National E-Prescription Networks: mTLS over REST/SOAP
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (US) -> US Pharmacy Systems: HL7 FHIR over HTTPS (OAuth 2.0)
- Platform -> Immutable Storage: GCP Bucket Lock for cryptographically signed AI audit logs

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Chosen for isolated regional deployments (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) ensuring data residency.
- WebRTC SFU: Enables real-time video/audio consultations with automatic degradation for rural low-bandwidth connections.
- OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect with MFA: Secures clinician and patient access alongside resilient session token caching.
- HL7 FHIR & REST/SOAP: Standardizes interoperability with US and EU external pharmacy systems.

## Rationale
Independent regional deployments on GCP completely prevent cross-border data leakage to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA. Furthermore, WebRTC bandwidth adaptation and Break-Glass authorization ensure uninterrupted emergency and rural care without sacrificing security.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency and compliance via isolated Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployments in Europe and the US.

## Key Elements
* Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians (People)
* National E-Prescription Networks (EU) and US Pharmacy Systems (External Systems)
* Web/Mobile Client Application (Flutter)
* Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy API Gateway
* Core Telehealth & Consent Container (Go)
* AI Symptom Checker Container (Python/FastAPI)
* Prescription Integration Container (Go)
* Immutable Storage (GCP Cloud Storage WORM)
* Regional GKE Clusters (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`) with Istio Service Mesh

## Relationships
* Client Application to API Gateway via HTTPS/gRPC with low-bandwidth adaptation (<300 kbit/s)
* API Gateway to Core Telehealth Container via gRPC
* Core Telehealth Container to AI Symptom Checker Container via gRPC
* AI Symptom Checker Container to Immutable Storage via HTTPS with local write-ahead buffering
* Prescription Integration Container to External Pharmacy Networks via mTLS and HTTPS (HL7 FHIR / EU national standards)

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Regional infrastructure ensuring data residency (R-05).
* Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) & Istio: Container orchestration and zero-trust network architecture (ZTNA).
* Go: Powers core telehealth and prescription integration services for high performance and operational simplicity.
* Python / FastAPI: Executes AI symptom checker inference and logging.
* Flutter / React: Cross-platform client supporting degraded-mode video.
* Envoy & GCP Cloud Load Balancing: Edge routing and low-bandwidth optimization.
* OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Observability for video degradation and AI audit metrics.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating regional data workloads while supporting low-bandwidth rural connections. Consolidating the backend tech stack to Go and Python reduces operational overhead while meeting stringent EU MDR auditability and interoperability standards.

Web/Mobile Client Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures regional data residency, HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and resilient access for rural users.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) & Licensed Clinicians
- Web/Mobile Client Application (Flutter / React Native)
- Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy API Gateway (Envoy & GCP Cloud Load Balancing)
- Core Telehealth & Consent Container (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Container (Python / FastAPI)
- Prescription Integration Container (Go)
- National E-Prescription Networks (EU) & US Pharmacy Systems
- WebRTC SFU Media Relay & Break-Glass Identity Provider (IdP)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Web/Mobile Client Application: Conducts consultations and manages consent [HTTPS / WebRTC]
- Web/Mobile Client Application -> Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy API Gateway: Sends encrypted API requests and streams media [TLS 1.3 / gRPC-Web / SRTP]
- Envoy API Gateway -> Core Telehealth, AI, and Prescription Containers: Routes internal traffic within regional data boundaries [gRPC]
- Core Telehealth Container -> National E-Prescription Networks / US Pharmacy Systems: Transmits e-prescriptions [HL7 FHIR / REST]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency constraints
- Flutter / React Native: Powers cross-platform client presentation and accessibility
- Go & Python (FastAPI): Implements high-performance microservices and AI workloads
- Envoy & GCP Cloud Load Balancing: Manages secure API ingress and routing
- SQLCipher & Platform Keychains: Secures offline PHI storage and volatile tokens
- libwebrtc: Handles adaptive media streaming for low-bandwidth connections (<300 kbit/s)

## Rationale
This architecture uses regional GCP deployments to strictly segregate EU and US health data while maintaining global compliance. Edge acceleration, gRPC-Web, and adaptive WebRTC media ensure high availability and low-bandwidth resilience for rural users.

Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency, low-bandwidth optimization, and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web/Mobile Client Application (Flutter / React)
- GCP External HTTP(S) Load Balancer & GCP Cloud Armor Security Policy
- Envoy Edge Proxy (Envoy with Ext-Authz, Localization, and WASM/Lua filters)
- Core Telehealth & Consent Container (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Container (Python / FastAPI)
- Prescription Integration Container (Go)
- Break-Glass Identity Provider (IdP) and Immutable Storage

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Client Application -> GCP External HTTP(S) Load Balancer: Sends client requests with low-bandwidth adaptation [HTTPS / gRPC (<300 kbit/s)]
- GCP External HTTP(S) Load Balancer -> GCP Cloud Armor Security Policy: Evaluates security rules [HTTPS]
- GCP Cloud Armor Security Policy -> Envoy Edge Proxy: Forwards filtered traffic [HTTPS]
- Envoy Edge Proxy -> Core Telehealth & Consent Container: Routes API requests [gRPC over mTLS]
- Envoy Edge Proxy -> AI Symptom Checker Container: Routes traceable AI requests [gRPC over mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- GCP Cloud Load Balancing & Cloud Armor: Edge routing and DDoS mitigation for regional separation
- Envoy Proxy: Traffic shaping, WASM/Lua filtering, W3C trace injection, and TLS 1.3 termination
- SPIFFE/SPIRE & GCP Certificate Authority Service: Zero-trust workload identity and automated certificate rotation
- Go & Python (FastAPI): High-performance backend services for telehealth logic and AI processing
- OpenTelemetry: Region-isolated distributed tracing enforcing data residency constraints

## Rationale
Regional GCP deployments (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) with edge Envoy gateways guarantee GDPR and HIPAA data residency compliance. Modular Envoy filters and gRPC over mTLS maintain strict security, zero-trust communication, and low-bandwidth resilience for rural users.

Core Telehealth & Consent Container.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency and GDPR/HIPAA compliance via GCP.

## Key Elements
*   **Clients:** Web/Mobile Client Application (Flutter / React)
*   **Edge:** Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy API Gateway (Envoy & GCP Cloud Load Balancing)
*   **Core Containers:** Core Telehealth & Consent Container (Go), AI Symptom Checker Container (Python / FastAPI), Prescription Integration Container (Go)
*   **Internal Components (Go):** Consent Management Component, Consultation Workflow Orchestrator, Regional Data Router, Consent Event Bus
*   **External/Data Services:** Regional Cloud SQL, WebRTC SFU Media Relay, Break-Glass Identity Provider (IdP), Immutable Storage, National E-Prescription Networks (EU), US Pharmacy Systems

## Relationships
*   *Web/Mobile Client* -> *Envoy API Gateway*: HTTPS / TLS 1.3
*   *Envoy API Gateway* -> *Core Telehealth & Consent Container*: gRPC / mTLS (SPIFFE/SPIRE)
*   *Core Telehealth & Consent Container* -> *AI Symptom Checker Container*: gRPC / mTLS with correlation IDs
*   *Regional Data Router* -> *Regional Cloud SQL*: SQL / TLS with regional CMEK
*   *Consent Management* -> *Consent Event Bus* -> *Workflow Orchestrator*: In-process Go channels / NATS

## Technology Stack
*   **Cloud Infrastructure:** Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for regional data residency.
*   **Orchestration & Deployment:** GKE Autopilot, ArgoCD, and Kustomize for GitOps-driven regional configuration.
*   **Backend & Inter-container:** Go with gRPC, Protocol Buffers, and mTLS via SPIFFE/SPIRE.
*   **Policy & Security:** Open Policy Agent (OPA) sidecar, GCP KMS (CMEK), and OAuth2/OIDC via Break-Glass IdP.
*   **Observability:** OpenTelemetry and Google Cloud Operations.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA) by isolating patient data regionally using GCP regions and CMEK keys. Go-based microservices with gRPC and OPA sidecars provide high performance, fine-grained consent enforcement, and robust traceability required for medical device compliance.

AI Symptom Checker Container.analysis:
## Overview
The AI Symptom Checker Container is a secure, low-latency microservice that provides automated urgency recommendations for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict regulatory compliance, data residency, and traceability under EU MDR and HIPAA standards.

## Key Elements
* API Router Component (FastAPI)
* Inference Engine Component (PyTorch / ONNX Runtime)
* Audit & Traceability Component
* Fallback Cache Component (Redis / Local LRU)
* Immutable Storage (Regional GCP Cloud Storage)

## Relationships
* API Router Component -> Inference Engine Component: In-process [Python function call] via gRPC ingestion
* API Router Component -> Fallback Cache Component: Queries cached profiles [In-process LRU / Redis client]
* Inference Engine Component -> Audit & Traceability Component: Dispatches audit payload [In-process queue]
* Audit & Traceability Component -> Immutable Storage: Writes cryptographically signed audit logs [HTTPS, regional GCP Cloud Storage]

## Technology Stack
* Python / FastAPI: High-performance asynchronous API routing and payload validation
* PyTorch / ONNX Runtime: Localized symptom analysis model execution
* GCP Cloud Run / GKE with KEDA: Serverless and containerized deployment with region-locked IAM
* GCP Cloud KMS: Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for at-rest data security

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees cross-border data residency compliance by isolating regional workloads in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`. It ensures high availability and accountability for rural users through local caching, encrypted disk buffering, and immutable audit logging.

Prescription Integration Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring secure, compliant cross-border medical operations.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web/Mobile Client Application (Flutter / React)
- Cloud Load Balancing & Envoy API Gateway (Envoy & GCP Cloud Load Balancing)
- Core Telehealth & Consent Container (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Container (Python / FastAPI)
- Prescription Integration Container (Go)
- External Systems: National E-Prescription Networks (EU), US Pharmacy Systems, WebRTC SFU Media Relay, Break-Glass Identity Provider (IdP), Immutable Storage
- GCP Infrastructure: GCP Pub/Sub, GCP Memorystore (Redis), GCP Cloud KMS, GCP Certificate Authority Service

## Relationships
- Prescription Integration Container -> National E-Prescription Networks (EU): Transmits e-prescriptions via mTLS and HTTPS (HL7 FHIR / EU standards)
- Prescription Integration Container -> US Pharmacy Systems: Transmits pharmacy requests via mTLS and HTTPS (HL7 FHIR)
- Web/Mobile Client Application -> Envoy API Gateway: Routes requests via HTTPS and WSS
- Prescription Integration Container -> GCP Pub/Sub: Manages asynchronous message queuing for retry handling
- Prescription Integration Container -> GCP Memorystore (Redis): Tracks idempotency keys via Redis protocol

## Technology Stack
- Go: Language for backend services and the Prescription Integration Container to ensure high concurrency and performance.
- Python / FastAPI: Framework for the AI symptom checker container supporting traceable medical device outputs.
- GCP Pub/Sub & Memorystore: Messaging and caching technologies providing asynchronous retry handling and idempotency persistence.
- mTLS & OAuth 2.0 (RFC 8693): Security protocols enforcing cryptographic token exchange and authenticated network transport.

## Rationale
The regional deployment model across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` strictly satisfies GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates. Asynchronous queuing, circuit breakers, and idempotency ledgers ensure high availability and prevent duplicate prescription dispatches during unstable network conditions.
